I am at the start of the season, and with my small area, long experience, and access to well irrigation, I will manage the land in a steady and practical way rather than take risks. I will use improved seed because I want more stable emergence and yield than old saved seed. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage since that is easier for me on a small plot and is enough for cotton establishment. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so the crop has enough strength for vegetative growth, boll setting, and fiber development without pushing too much weak growth. Because I have well irrigation, I will plan several irrigations through the season, mainly around establishment, flowering, and boll formation, depending on moisture. I will also expect to spray several times because cotton usually needs pest control during the growing season. With this approach, I am aiming for a stable, manageable cotton crop and a reasonable yield from my small field.
